newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish hostages free, Yemen informs Warsaw.
newsitem.headline: Polish hostages free, Yemen informs Warsaw.

text.p: A group of Polish hostages held by tribesmen in Yemen since last week have been freed, the foreign ministry in Warsaw quoted Yemeni authorities as saying on Tuesday.

"Yemen's foreign and interior ministries say they are already free," Przemyslaw Antoniewicz, deputy head of the ministry's press office, told Reuters, but could give no details of how they were freed.
He said Poland's ambassador in Yemen, Krzysztof Suprowicz, had not yet seen the hostages in person.

The tourists -- three men and two women aged between 50 and 64 -- were kidnapped on their way to archaeological sites last week by members of the Al al-Masni tribe in the Khawlan area, about 65 km (40 miles) east of the capital Sanaa.
Since then Yemen authorities have been in negotiations with the kidnappers to secure the hostages' release.
On Friday, the tribesmen fired grenades at military forces who had surrounded them, killing three soldiers and wounding five.
In recent years, tribes in Yemen with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped foreigners to use in bargaining with the authorities, often over land or water issues.
Polish officials have declined to name the hostages.
A leading member of a club devoted to exotic foreign travel told Gazeta Wyborcza newspaper she believed they were from the Polish Explorers's Society.

Biologist Zofia Sikorska-Piwowska said their reported ages and sexes fitted those of five society members who had left on December 10 for a tour of Yemen, Ethiopia and Sudan and who included a freelance journalist and a couple of physicists.
